segments.text: The nineties icon is back — the Tata Sierra, starting at just eleven and a half lakh, ex-showroom.
Under the bonnet — a one-sixty horsepower turbo-petrol with two-fifty-five newtons of torque, or a punchy diesel.
Top trims add Level-two driver assist with twenty-two features, a panoramic sunroof, and a thirteen-speaker Dolby system.
Six airbags, a huge six-twenty-litre boot, a twelve-point-three-inch screen — the icon properly grew up.
But remember, it's front-wheel drive, not a hardcore off-roader. Sierra or Creta? Comment one or two, then like, share, and subscribe.
